stories.registration-problem: {{cast.user}} wants {{cast.assistant}} to draft visit notes. The {{cast.resource}} has never heard of {{cast.assistant}}, and {{cast.company}} cannot pre-register every tool a clinician tries.
stories.idea: {{cast.assistant}} publishes a JSON file at {{cast.clientUrl}}; the address is its client id. The server reads the file at request time.
stories.document: The file at {{cast.clientUrl}} names {{cast.client}}, lists the callback it will use and carries no secret, since the file is public.
stories.strict: Because anyone can choose the address, {{cast.company}}'s server reads it with care: https only, no private addresses, no redirects, a size cap, and an id that matches the address.
stories.direction1: The lab acts as {{cast.client}} and real PingFederate as {{cast.company}}'s sign-in server. Whether PingFederate takes a URL client id is not verified, and no mock stands in for it.
stories.probe: The probe gives PingFederate {{cast.client}}'s address. A move to sign-in means it was accepted; HTTP 400 means no enabled policy matches the address.
stories.direction2: The lab is now {{cast.company}}'s teaching sign-in server. {{cast.user}} sees a consent screen built from {{cast.client}}'s file and approves; the access token is the lab's opaque teaching value.
stories.refusals: A tool pretending to be {{cast.client}} with a mismatched id, a secret in the file, an oversize body or a redirect is stopped at a named check; a reused code fails.
stories.close: {{cast.company}} avoids a registration step and relies on how strictly the server reads the file. Reset clears the lab.
